handsOnEffort.basis: Assuming the developer has a Slack workspace, creates an app in the console, configures redirect URIs and scopes, and links credentials into Composio.

summary.text: Apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines; unlisted distributed apps are not.
summary.quote: Unlike unlisted distributed apps, apps listed in the Slack Marketplace are reviewed against our requirements & guidelines

triggers.text: Submitting the app for a Slack Marketplace listing, which Slack recommends for apps intended for commercial distribution.
triggers.quote: Apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace to develop in; Slack recommends setting up a developer sandbox if you don't have one.

redirectRules.text: The redirect_uri, and any Redirect URL configured under OAuth & Permissions, must use HTTPS.
redirectRules.quote: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions. A Redirect URL must also use HTTPS.

redirectRules.text: The redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management, and a Redirect URL can't contain an anchor (#).
redirectRules.quote: Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management. A Redirect URL can not contain an anchor (#).

steps.title: Create a Slack App
steps.action: Create a new Slack app in the App Management console.
steps.actorReason: Requires logging into the developer's Slack account and creating resources in the dashboard.
steps.text: Create the Slack app; a new app resides in one workspace until you distribute it, listed or unlisted.
steps.quote: When you create a Slack app, it resides in one workspace. You can also distribute Slack apps in either listed or unlisted fashion.

steps.title: Determine and Draft Scopes
steps.action: List the required bot and user scopes for your application.
steps.where: Local development environment or app manifest
steps.actorReason: An agent can analyze tool requirements and draft the necessary scope list without accessing provider accounts.
steps.text: Identify the minimum necessary bot and user scopes required by your integration.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URLs
steps.action: Add the Composio redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions.
steps.where: Slack App Management under OAuth & Permissions
steps.actorReason: An agent can provide the exact redirect URI value while the developer inputs it into the Slack dashboard.
steps.text: Configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions.
steps.quote: Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions.

steps.title: Create Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.action: Create a custom auth config for Slack in the Composio dashboard.
steps.actorReason: An agent can guide the dashboard configuration steps while the developer interacts with the UI.
steps.text: Create the auth config in the Composio dashboard and enter the required credential fields.
steps.quote: 1. Click Create Auth Config 2. Select the toolkit 3. Choose the auth scheme (OAuth2, API Key, Bearer Token, etc.) 4. Follow the dashboard instructions for the required credential fields

steps.title: Copy Credentials into Composio
steps.action: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Slack and enter them into Composio.
steps.where: Slack App Management Basic Information & Composio Dashboard
steps.actorReason: Viewing sensitive client secrets requires human access to the provider console.
steps.text: Extract your app credentials from Slack and store them in your Composio auth configuration.
steps.quote: register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.action: In the app's dashboard, scroll to Share Your App with Other Workspaces under Manage Distribution, complete the checklist, and click Activate Public Distribution. Without this, only the app's own workspace can install it.
steps.actorReason: Changing an app's distribution is a console action taken by the app's owner.
steps.text: To let other workspaces install the app, complete the checklist under Share Your App with Other Workspaces and click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.quote: Scroll to Share Your App with Other Workspaces within the Manage Distribution section. 3. Ensure all items in the supplied checklist are completed. 4. Click Activate Public Distribution.

steps.title: Connect a Test Account
steps.action: Initiate the OAuth flow to connect a test workspace account.
steps.where: Composio Connect Link or application auth flow
steps.actorReason: Authorizing permissions and installing the app on a workspace requires human approval.
steps.text: Test the connection by completing the OAuth authorization flow in your target workspace.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace Review (Optional)
steps.action: Submit the app for review if commercial distribution is needed.
steps.actorReason: Submitting applications for formal third-party security and marketplace review requires human administrative action.
steps.text: Submit your app for listing in the Slack Marketplace if you intend to distribute it commercially.
steps.quote: Apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

faq.question: How does Composio handle my Slack data?
faq.answer: Composio executes API calls on behalf of your connected account. All data is encrypted and subject to a 30-day retention policy. Authentication tokens are encrypted at rest and scoped to the permissions you grant during the OAuth flow. For full details on data handling, retention, and third-party data practices, see our [Privacy Policy](https://composio.dev/privacy).

faq.question: How do I set up custom OAuth credentials for Slack?
faq.answer: For a step-by-step guide on creating and configuring your own Slack OAuth credentials with Composio, see [How to create OAuth credentials for Slack](https://composio.dev/auth/slack).

faq.question: When do users see "This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace…"?
faq.answer:
When a member of a Slack workspace tries to install a non-Marketplace app.

**How to resolve:** Disable **Require apps from Slack Marketplace** in the workspace's app management settings:

`Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings`

faq.question: Why am I being asked to submit a request during auth?
faq.answer: Because **Require approved apps** is enabled in the workspace's **App Management Settings**. Slack is asking for admin/owner approval before completing the install.

faq.question: How can a workspace member complete the connection without asking for permissions or approvals?
faq.answer:
Two ways:

- Disable both **Require apps from Slack Marketplace** and **Require approved apps** in the workspace's app management settings.
- Use the workspace's own OAuth app, which is recommended and safest. See [How to create OAuth credentials for Slack](https://composio.dev/auth/slack).

faq.question: Where can I find Slack's available scopes?
Why am I getting a redirect URI mismatch error?
faq.answer: Update the redirect URL in your Slack App under OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs.

faq.question: How do I set up Slack event webhooks?
faq.answer: With Composio-managed Slack credentials, the webhook endpoint is already provisioned, so just create the trigger. If you bring your own Slack OAuth app, see [Custom OAuth webhooks](https://docs.composio.dev/docs/setting-up-triggers/custom-oauth-webhooks).
